name: Component-by-Component Ablation on Jitter, State Transitions, and Geometric Snapping
provenance: SIMULATED (Parameter Sweeps across 6 Noise Levels x 30 Seeds per Subsystem)

configurations.notes: Full stabilization, state filtering, scale normalization, and geometric snapping enabled.
Removing hysteresis leads to severe limit-cycle chatter at the decision boundary.

configurations.rms_jitter_mm: 3.176 mm (0.0% jitter reduction on active/moving paths)
configurations.notes: Without continuous interpolation, active motion suffers high-frequency tremor.

configurations.rms_jitter_mm: 1.193 mm (stationary), but drag latency increases during rapid strokes
configurations.notes: Static LERP dampens noise but introduces lag at high velocities and micro-drift when resting.
Pinch distance varies by 70.0% between 30 cm and 100 cm, breaking universal gesture thresholds.
Without magnetic capture, human motor imprecision leaves gaps at vertex intersections.
Raw unconditioned pipeline: severe jitter, rapid pinch chatter, distance sensitivity, poor precision.

verdict: Sensitivity sweeps confirm each component is mathematically necessary across 180 runs per module: Hysteresis prevents chatter (85.6% mean reduction), Adaptive smoothing suppresses jitter (52.4% mean reduction), Scale normalization guarantees distance invariance (0% vs 70% error), and Snapping ensures geometric capture (79.7% mean error reduction, 84.5% capture rate).
